active_scrape.description: Data acquired by running scraper scripts (slow, respectful delays)

cached_static.description: Pre-scraped data snapshots, read directly from disk

reference_data.description: Static reference data (value charts, lookup tables)

gm_executives.notes: General Manager and executive tenure data for all 32 NFL teams. Script runs ~3 min with Selenium.

nflreadpy.access_pattern: import nflreadpy as nfl; data = nfl.load_*()
nflreadpy.notes: Primary data source - professionally maintained with daily automated updates

coverage.notes: Player stats incomplete for 2012 Weeks 1-11 and 2024 Weeks 16-22. Team stats are most complete.

cached_nfl_stats.recommendation: Keep - most complete team stats dataset
cached_nfl_stats.notes: Comprehensive player/team statistics - 468+ fields. Team stats complete through 2024 Super Bowl.

cached_nfl_scraper.recommendation: Keep - essential for play-level and drive analysis
cached_nfl_scraper.notes: Individual play-level data. Most detailed dataset available. Includes preseason.

cached_historical_stats.best_for: Historical game logs and career stats 1970-2016
cached_historical_stats.notes: Career stats and game logs by position. Complements modern datasets.

draft_value_charts.notes: Four draft value charts available for comparison/analysis: (1) Jimmy Johnson (classic, most widely used), (2) Rich Hill (modern update), (3) Fitzgerald-Spielberger (highest valuations), (4) Harvard (empirically derived). Different methodologies and scales allow for robust trade analysis.

jimmy_johnson.description: Classic Jimmy Johnson chart (created by Mike McCoy) - most widely used by NFL teams historically

rich_hill.description: Rich Hill's updated draft value chart - modern recalibration

fitzgerald_spielberger.description: Fitzgerald-Spielberger draft value chart - similar scale to Jimmy Johnson but different curve

harvard.description: Harvard Sports Analytics Collective draft value chart - empirically derived from actual player performance
